blocks.text: The same idea lifts to grids. Instead of the sum of everything before index `i`, each cell stores the sum of the whole rectangle above and to the left of it.
Each cell adds its own value to the rectangle above and the rectangle to the left — but those two overlap, so the shared corner must be subtracted back out:
That add-add-subtract is **inclusion–exclusion**. Two overlapping regions cover their intersection twice, so one copy is removed.
To get the sum of a rectangle, start from the big rectangle ending at the bottom-right corner, cut away the strip above and the strip to the left, then add back the corner removed twice:
Four lookups, whatever the rectangle's size. A 1000 x 1000 region costs the same as a single cell.

Just as the 1D version had a leading zero, the 2D version has an all-zero first row **and** first column. They exist so that queries touching the top or left edge need no special case — the formula reads a zero instead of running out of bounds.

items: **Build:** O(R x C) time and space.

blocks.text: If inclusion–exclusion feels slippery, draw a 4 x 4 grid and shade the four rectangles by hand. It becomes obvious quickly and stays obvious.
